problem_markdown: For the side lengths $a,b,c$ of a nondegenerate triangle, prove $a^2b(a-b)+b^2c(b-c)+c^2a(c-a)\ge0$ and determine equality.
solutions_markdown:
Write $a=y+z$, $b=z+x$, $c=x+y$ with $x,y,z>0$. Expanding the target expression gives
$$2\bigl(xy^3+yz^3+zx^3-xyz(x+y+z)\bigr)
=2xyz\left(\frac{y^2}{z}+\frac{z^2}{x}+\frac{x^2}{y}-x-y-z\right).$$
Cauchy–Schwarz gives
$$\frac{y^2}{z}+\frac{z^2}{x}+\frac{x^2}{y}\ge\frac{(x+y+z)^2}{x+y+z}=x+y+z.$$
Equality requires $y/z=z/x=x/y$, forcing $x=y=z$ because they are positive. Thus equality holds exactly when $a=b=c$.
